### 0452111 Jurisprudence of Purification, Prayer and Fasting (3 Credit Hours)
Introduction to jurisprudence doctrines; their founders and their methods of deduction; definition of Fiqh; purity; ablution; washing; types of water; menses; prayers; prayer of travelers, Friday prayer, prayers of feasts; prayer of the sick; funeral prayer. Jurisprudence of Fasting; definition; pillars of fasting; its time; I'tikaf, definition and conditions.

### 0452212 Jurisprudence of Alms and Pilgrimage (3 Credit Hours)
The jurisprudence of Alms; its concept, legislation, conditions, the kinds of wealth which apply to alms, the relationship between alms, tax and ways of spending alms. The course also discusses the Jurisprudence of Hajj (pilgrimage): its concept, legislation and rules. This covers its time, kinds of Hajj, to do hajj instead of others, and the rules of Omrah.

### 0401131 Dialogue in Islam (3 Credit Hours)
This course includes the meaning of dialogue, its importance, objective, methodologies, principles, methods, ethics, the conversed, and dialogue with Muslims and non-Muslims. Rules for the foregoing are derived from the Qur’an and the prophetic Sunnah.

### 0401202 Biography of the Rightly-Guided Caliph (3 Credit Hours)
This course highlights the most important events and developments in political administration and military both domestic and foreign affairs of the Islamic state. It addresses the issue of how can we make benefit of these events in our contemporary time by analyzing the methodology of every caliph in implementing Islam.

### 0401236 Da’wah texts in the Qur’an and the Sunnah (3 Credit Hours)
This course touches on selected Qur’anic and prophetic texts which clarify Da’wah objective, its importance and that it is the prophets’ and messengers’- peace be upon them- career, the reward of those who do it, the tools of Da’wah and its methodologies. It also reviews Da’wah methodologies especially those adopted by the last prophet - peace be upon him - through the Qur’an and the prophetic Sunnah.

### 0401237 Islamic studies in the human psyche (3 Credit Hours)
